nrIncident.message:
A fault with the signalling system between Fareham and Southampton Central means fewer trains will run between these stations. Trains running between these stations may be cancelled, delayed by up to 35 minutes or revised.
Disruption is expected until 11:30.
Great Western Railway customer advice:
As trains are still running you should travel as normal and catch your intended train.
If your train is cancelled, you may travel on either of the two services before, or two services after, your original train. If these are peak services or less flexible, you can still travel with your original ticket, at no extra cost.

South Western Railway customer advice:
Long distance and mainline services:
Train services from Portsmouth stations to London Waterloo via Eastleigh / Basingstoke are not affected by this issue, but may be delayed due to trains awaiting arrival into Fareham station.
Delays of up to 45 minutes are expected.
Train services between Portsmouth stations and London Waterloo via Guildford are not directly affected by this issue, but may be delayed due to congestion in the Portsmouth area caused by the delays in the Fareham area.

Southern customer advice:
If you are travelling between Fareham and Southampton Central, in either direction, your journey will be delayed and you will likely need to use a different operator to complete your journey. This is due to a signalling fault in the Netley area.
Southern Services that normally run between Brighton and Southampton Central will run between Brighton and Portsmouth or Bognor Regis instead. If you require stations between Fratton and Southampton, please change at Fratton and use South Western Railway or Great Western Railway services to complete your journey.
Please note that using an alternative route will take longer than usual. make sure to leave at least an extra 40 minutes to reach your destination.
For the latest information, please use station boards or online journey planners.

• Alternative Southern services between Brighton and Barnham / Havant and Portsmouth Harbour

Stay up to date on the move with Southern’s WhatsApp channel. Live updates are available Monday to Friday, 07:00–21:00.
Can you tell me more about the incident?
This fault has been identified as a track circuit failure. Track circuits are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. If one fails, the signalling system may show that a section of track is occupied even when there isn’t a train there. This means signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and request verbal permission from the signaller before continuing past the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely should they see anything ahead of them.
This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.
